skill.name: lark-slides
skill.description: Create, read, and manage Lark Slides presentations using Lark CLI commands and SML XML templates.
skill.summary: Build and edit Lark Slides presentations with XML-based slide creation, media upload, reading, and deletion workflows.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are documentation backticks, XML namespace URLs, and long XML strings rather than executable payloads. I confirmed the parent-directory shared-skill references because they instruct the agent to read outside the package boundary. The skill also contains legitimate but sensitive workflows for uploading local files to Lark and deleting slide content.

remediation.suggestion: Vendor the required shared instructions inside this package or reference a reviewed marketplace dependency instead of using parent-directory reads.

remediation.issue: Local file upload to Lark Drive
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, display each selected relative path, and refuse absolute or parent-directory paths before upload.
Ask for confirmation before fetching user-provided URLs and store downloads only in a user-approved working directory.
Require explicit confirmation before delete operations and preserve the fetched XML content before replacing a slide.

semantic_findings.title: Local File Upload to Lark Drive
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to upload local image files to Lark and replace XML image paths with returned file tokens. This is legitimate for slides, but it can expose local files if paths are not explicitly chosen by the user.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Image Download Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to download web images to the current directory before uploading them to Lark. Fetching arbitrary user-provided URLs can retrieve untrusted content and should require confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance explicitly says to download web images before upload when users provide image links. It is a legitimate workflow, but arbitrary URL fetches are security-sensitive.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Slide Deletion Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill supports deleting slides and replacing whole slides when element-level edits are unavailable. This can permanently remove presentation content if executed without clear user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines document irreversible deletion and batch deletion patterns. The feature is intended, but it needs explicit user approval before execution.

content.value_statement: Teams need a reliable way to build Lark Slides without guessing XML structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Lark CLI workflows for slide creation, reading, media upload, and deletion.
actual_capabilities: Create new Lark Slides presentations with one or more XML-defined slides.
Read existing presentation XML through xml_presentations.get workflows.
Add slides to existing presentations with xml_presentation.slide.create.
Delete slides with documented safeguards and revision handling.
Upload local images to Lark Drive and use returned file tokens.
Provide XML templates for covers, content pages, data cards, and image layouts.
limitations: Requires installed and authenticated lark-cli with the needed Lark scopes.
Does not edit individual slide elements; changes often require recreating a full slide.
Image workflows are limited to local files or uploaded Lark file tokens.
Complex chart and table XML still require careful schema review.

use_cases.title: Build Weekly Business Reviews
use_cases.description: Create structured review decks with consistent layouts, metrics pages, and speaker notes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Sales Enablement Decks
use_cases.description: Turn product positioning and proof points into Lark Slides presentations with reusable page templates.

use_cases.title: Automate Slide Maintenance
use_cases.description: Read existing presentation XML, add new pages, upload images, and remove outdated slides.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a five-slide Lark Slides deck about [topic] for [audience]. Propose an outline first, then create it after approval.

prompt_templates.title: Add a New Slide
prompt_templates.prompt: Add one slide to this Lark presentation: [presentation link]. Match the current style and show the planned slide before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Use Local Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Lark Slides presentation using these local images: [relative paths]. Confirm each file path before upload.

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild a Slide Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Update slide [slide description] in [presentation link]. Read the full XML, preserve existing elements, create the replacement, then delete the old slide after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Create a quarterly review deck for product leaders.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a slide outline, asks for approval, creates the Lark presentation, and returns the presentation identifier and link.

output_examples.input: Add a customer quote slide to an existing deck.
output_examples.output: The skill reads the presentation context, drafts a matching slide, inserts it in the requested position, and reports the new slide status.

output_examples.input: Replace a slide image with a local chart file.
output_examples.output: The skill confirms the local file path, uploads the image, rebuilds the target slide, and explains any changed slide identifiers.

best_practices: Confirm the outline, target audience, and style before creating slides.
Use user identity by default, and confirm bot identity before using it.
Review generated XML with schema references before running write operations.
anti_patterns: Do not delete slides before creating and checking replacements.
Do not use external image URLs directly in slide XML.
Do not upload local files unless the user selected the files.

faq.question: What does this skill need before it can run?
faq.answer: It needs lark-cli installed, an authenticated Lark account, and the required Slides or Drive scopes.

faq.question: Can it create a complete presentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a new Lark Slides presentation and add XML-defined slides.

faq.question: Can it edit one text box or image in place?
faq.answer: No. The documented XML API works at slide level, so many edits require rebuilding a whole slide.

faq.question: Can it use images from my computer?
faq.answer: Yes, but only after you confirm CWD-relative paths that should be uploaded to Lark.

faq.question: Does it support Lark wiki presentation links?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation explains resolving wiki links to the real presentation token before editing.

faq.question: Is deletion reversible?
faq.answer: No. Slide deletion is documented as irreversible, so the user should confirm before any delete operation.
